TASK

## Company Name (TICKER) `[Category]`

RULES

- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.

content:
## CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (CRWD) `[Software & SaaS]`
- CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Okta gained about 4% during September 23 trading while the First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF gained 1%; 24/7 Wall St. attributed the move to a cybersecurity-sector rally rather than a company-specific announcement. (24/7 Wall St.)
- Bank of America raised its price target to **$260**, citing AI-related attack surfaces as a cybersecurity growth catalyst. (Bank of America note)
- Wedbush initiated coverage with an **Outperform** rating, citing **25% year-over-year ARR growth** and a **51% increase in net-new ARR** in the latest reported quarter. (Wedbush note)
- CrowdStrike’s latest reported quarter included **$1.47 billion of revenue**, **$333 million of net-new ARR**, **$2.29 billion of Falcon Flex ARR**, and full-year ARR guidance of **$1.35 billion**. (company results)

## Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (PANW) `[Software & SaaS]`
- Palo Alto Networks rose with CrowdStrike, Okta, and other cybersecurity shares; the First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF gained **1%** during the session. (24/7 Wall St.)
- Palo Alto Networks and Palantir were identified as stocks flashing technical buy signals after September 23 trading. (Investor’s Business Daily)
- Palo Alto Networks had announced a new **AI defense service** before the September 23 session; the company’s next quarterly results were listed for **November 12, 2026**. (AD HOC NEWS)

## Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) `[AI Infrastructure]`
- Palantir rose alongside cybersecurity and AI-related software stocks while the Nasdaq-100 and broader large-cap technology sector declined; 24/7 Wall St. described the move as part of an AI-adjacent enterprise-software bid. (24/7 Wall St.)
- Palantir advanced **3.7%** to **$191.79** in Investor’s Business Daily’s September 23 market recap and moved above a short-term high of **$118.37**. (Investor’s Business Daily)
- Palantir and Palo Alto Networks were identified as stocks flashing technical buy signals after the session. (Investor’s Business Daily)

## BP p.l.c. (BP) `[Energy]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.
- Crude oil rose **1.8% to $92.16 per barrel** on September 23 after five consecutive sessions of declines; the energy sector was reported as the only sector to advance in the session. (Investor’s Business Daily; US Stock Today)

## Fortinet, Inc. (FTNT) `[Software & SaaS]`
- Fortinet rose with cybersecurity peers; a September 23 market recap listed Fortinet higher by **2.6%** while Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike each gained about **5%**. (WOLF Financial)
- Josh Brown identified Fortinet, CrowdStrike, and Palo Alto Networks as cybersecurity stocks he considered attractive and cited Fortinet’s trading range of **$150–$175**, a 50-day moving average near **$160**, and a 200-day moving average near **$114**. (Ritholtz CEO Josh Brown)

## Equinor ASA (EQNR) `[Energy]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.
- Crude oil prices rebounded on September 23 after five sessions of declines; Reuters reported world crude prices above **$100 per barrel** amid attention on possible U.S.-Iranian presidential talks in New York. (Reuters)

## Western Digital Corporation (WDC) `[Memory & Interconnect]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.

## Salesforce, Inc. (CRM) `[Software & SaaS]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.
- The broader market declined as the 10-year Treasury yield rose **15 basis points to 5.11%**, a level described as the highest since 2007; this was cited as a factor affecting large-cap technology stocks. (Investor’s Business Daily)

## ServiceNow, Inc. (NOW) `[Software & SaaS]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.
- The broader market declined as the 10-year Treasury yield rose **15 basis points to 5.11%**, while cybersecurity and selected AI-related software stocks advanced. (Investor’s Business Daily; 24/7 Wall St.)

## T-Mobile US, Inc. (TMUS) `[Wireless & Mobile]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.
- T-Mobile was listed among Nasdaq-100 stocks advancing on September 23, with an intraday gain of **1.80%** in a market-data recap that also identified cybersecurity and AI-related stocks as leaders. (TechFlow Post)

## Okta, Inc. (OKTA) `[Software & SaaS]`
- Scotiabank raised its price target from **$165 to $190** and maintained a **Sector Outperform** rating; MarketBeat reported that Okta shares rose **3.7%** during Wednesday trading. (Scotiabank note, via MarketBeat)
- MarketBeat listed Okta’s consensus rating as **Moderate Buy** and its consensus price target as **$177.61**. (MarketBeat)
- Okta rose with CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks in a cybersecurity-sector rally; the First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF gained **1%** during the session. (24/7 Wall St.)
